name: BASS (Burning and Suppression of Solids)
fuels: PMMA thin flat samples (100 to 400 um)
measurements: Flame spread rate by image analysis, extinction limits
key_result: Thin PMMA sheets burned in the ISS glovebox across oxygen and flow velocity; spread rate by image analysis.
note: Verified against NASA/TM-20210011385 BASS-II Summary Report. ISS MSG flow duct, PMMA thin sheets, flow 0-42 cm/s.

name: BASS-II (PMMA cylinders)
measurements: Spread rate by tracking the flame leading edge; extinction
data_access: NASA PSI; supplementary tables of the paper
key_result: In microgravity, spread rate first rises then falls with opposed flow, and flames persist at lower oxygen (about 17%) than in 1g (about 18%).
note: Values from Link et al. 2018 main text; pressure is ISS cabin pressure (value not stated in the main text).

name: SoFIE (Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction)
fuels: PMMA cylinders, spheres and slabs (see source)
measurements: Ignition, spread and extinction of solid fuels
key_result: Studies solid-fuel ignition and extinction over a wider pressure and oxygen range than the glovebox experiments.
note: Verified against NASA NTRS 20200000361 (SoFIE Project on ISS in CIR). Tested PMMA cylinders, spheres, and slabs.

name: Saffire I to VI
fuels: Fabric and other materials, samples up to 40.6 by 94 cm
measurements: Flame spread, flame power, large-scale fire behaviour
key_result: First large-scale fires in space; reported cloth spread rates of about 1 to 2 mm/s in concurrent flow and a flame power near 1.2 kW in the first test.
note: Verified against NASA NTRS 20170008805 (Saffire large-scale spacecraft fire experiments). Sample size 94 x 40.6 cm fiberglass-cotton fabric.

name: LUCI (Lunar Combustion Investigation)
key_result: First extended-duration (over 25 seconds) combustion tests in simulated lunar gravity.
note: Verified against NASA NTRS 20250010653 (LUCI sounding rocket lunar combustion). Extended-duration >25 s simulated lunar gravity tests.

name: ACME (Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments)
key_result: Studies gas-phase flames and soot in microgravity; does not report solid-fuel flame spread rates.
note: Verified against NASA GRC ACME ISRD (ACME-SRD-001.B). Microgravity gaseous flame research in CIR using spherical porous burners.

name: ZARM drop tower: thin PMMA with barriers (this dashboard's data)
fuels: PMMA thin film, 75 um, with aluminium or stainless-steel barriers
measurements: Global flame spread rate, temperature and heat-flux profiles, barrier gap flammability
key_result: Global spread rate rose from about 2.4 to 6.3 mm/s as oxygen rose from 21.6 to 36% (pressure falling from 103 to 62 kPa); barriers reduce spread.
note: Ranges computed from the 22-experiment table; duration is the length of the longest recorded series, not the drop time.

name: NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 (upward flame propagation)
key_result: NASA's main material flammability screening method; upward burning in normal gravity only.
note: Verified against NASA NTRS 20070018178 (NASA-STD-6001 upward flame propagation standard evaluation).

name: Piloted ignition of PMMA in exploration atmospheres
key_result: Piloted ignition of PMMA studied in the proposed exploration cabin environment of 52.7 to 58.6 kPa and 30 to 34% oxygen.
note: Verified against NASA NTRS 20080013149 (Piloted ignition delay of PMMA in exploration atmospheres 52.7-58.6 kPa, 30-34% O2).

name: Rotating suborbital capsule for lunar-gravity fire tests (planned)
key_result: About 120 s at 0.165 g with about 34% oxygen and 8.2 psi: a starting point for lunar habitat flammability experiments.
note: Verified against NASA Science Fire Detection White Paper (p. 6, Table 1). Rotating capsule ~120 s at 0.165 g, 34% O2, 8.2 psi.

name: FLARE (Flammability Limits at Reduced-g Experiment)
measurements: Flammability limits of materials at reduced gravity
key_result: Project to measure material flammability limits in reduced gravity; a 2021 workshop reviewed the technology needs.
note: Verified against NASA NTRS 20210021318 (FLARE 2021 workshop). Development of flammability limits and testing at reduced gravity.

name: FLEX and FLEX-2 (Flame Extinguishment Experiment)
fuels: Heptane, methanol, and decane fuel droplets (1.5 to 5 mm)
measurements: Droplet burning rates, radiative and diffusive extinction limits, cool-flame transitions, CO2 and He suppression
key_result: Suppression by chamber dilution with CO2 and helium demonstrated in MDCA/CIR; discovered sustained low-temperature quasi-steady cool flame burning.
note: Verified against NASA/TM-20150022123 (FLEX droplet combustion suppression in MDCA).

name: SAME, SAME-R, and DAFT (Smoke & Dust Measurement)
fuels: Pyrolyzed spacecraft materials (Kapton, Teflon, silicone, cotton), Arizona test dust
measurements: Particulate size distribution (15 to 500 nm), ionization detector response, light obscuration, smoke-dust discrimination
key_result: Characterized microgravity smoke particulate agglomeration; demonstrated dual-parameter sensing to distinguish spacecraft smoke from lunar/Martian dust.
note: Verified against NASA Fire Detection White Paper (pp. 2-5). SAME/DAFT particle size distribution and smoke-dust discrimination.

name: BRE and CFI-G (Burning Rate Emulator & Cool Flames with Gases)
fuels: Gaseous fuels (ethylene, methane, propane) over porous flat and spherical burners
measurements: Burning rate emulation of solid materials, high-oxygen extinction limits up to 85% O2, radiative extinction, cool flame dynamics
key_result: Emulated solid material flammability with gaseous fuel burners; mapped high-oxygen extinction limits up to 85% O2 in CIR/ACME.
note: Verified against NASA NTRS 20140009169 (ACME/BRE Burning Rate Emulator investigation).

name: FM2 (Flammability of Materials on the Moon)
measurements: Optical cameras (color, size, intensity, spread rate), thermocouples, O2, CO2 sensors
key_result: First-ever combustion test on lunar surface (1/6g); models & drop tower tests indicate lower O2 flammability boundary than 1g.
note: Autonomous 25 kg sealed chamber (28.5x28.5x38.5 cm) on lunar lander; tests NASA-STD-6001 validity at 1/6 g.
